summary: Installed and configured a persistent iptables/ip6tables host firewall on node1 (Alpine Linux) that accepts SSH (22) and TCP 8080, allows loopback/established traffic and ICMP echo, and rejects all other inbound connections with icmp-port-unreachable. Rules were saved via OpenRC (/etc/iptables/rules-save, /etc/iptables/rules6-save) and the iptables/ip6tables services were added to the default runlevel. Verified functionally before and after a full node reboot (new boot_id confirmed a real restart), with firewall rules, service state, and SSH all recovering automatically and correctly.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Alpine 3.23) and confirmed no firewall/iptables was installed
Installed iptables and ip6tables packages via apk
Configured INPUT chain: ACCEPT lo, ACCEPT ESTABLISHED/RELATED, ACCEPT tcp/22, ACCEPT tcp/8080, ACCEPT icmp echo-request, REJECT all else, policy DROP (mirrored for ip6tables)
Persisted rules with /etc/init.d/iptables save and /etc/init.d/ip6tables save, added both services to the default OpenRC runlevel, started both services
Captured baseline boot_id and functional proof (8080 allowed, SSH allowed, arbitrary port 9999 rejected)
Issued native reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (new value after reboot), confirming a genuine restart
Re-verified firewall rules were auto-restored, iptables/ip6tables services started, sshd running, and re-ran functional port tests (8080 allowed, 22 allowed, 9999 rejected) matching baseline

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall installed and enabled on boot
evidence.summary: iptables/ip6tables packages installed, rules saved to /etc/iptables/rules-save and rules6-save, services added to default runlevel and started

evidence.requirement: SSH permitted, TCP 8080 permitted, unrelated inbound rejected (pre-reboot baseline)
evidence.summary: iptables/ip6tables rule listing shows ACCEPT for tcp/22 and tcp/8080, REJECT for all else; live nc test confirms 8080 and 22 reachable while port 9999 is rejected (exit 1) not timed out

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and boot identity change
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured as 10543e2b-26a1-4791-b491-a83fca0cd247; reboot command acknowledged (stream closed as node went down); post-recovery boot_id read as 3139c901-461c-488c-b5ad-534dda1b1574, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of firewall, services, and functional behavior
evidence.summary: After reboot, iptables/ip6tables services show started with rules identical to pre-reboot config, sshd is running and listening, and live port tests again confirm 8080/22 allowed and 9999 rejected
